subject: Business Models
title: Tokenized Real Estate
description: A fast breakdown of Tokenized Real Estate for builders.

hook.text: You can now buy $50 of a Manhattan apartment building. Tokenization splits real estate into digital shares.

buildup.text: Blockchain tokens represent fractional ownership of real assets: buildings, art, and even farmland.

discovery.text: Tokenization makes illiquid assets liquid. Instead of selling an entire building, you sell thousands of tiny shares.

twist.text: Regulatory uncertainty slows adoption. Are tokens securities? Different countries give different answers.

climax.text: If tokenization scales, millions of people could own pieces of assets previously reserved for the ultra-wealthy.

punchline.text: $50 for a slice of Manhattan. Tokenization democratizes real estate ownership.

quiz.question: What does tokenized real estate enable?
options: Fractional ownership of properties through digital tokens

details.summary: Tokenized real estate divides property ownership into blockchain-based digital tokens that can be bought and sold in small fractions. A million-dollar building can be split into 10,000 tokens of $100 each, allowing anyone to invest in real estate with minimal capital and trade their position easily.
details.whyItMatters: Real estate tokenization could democratize access to property investment by eliminating minimum investment thresholds, reducing transaction friction.
takeaways: Properties are divided into blockchain tokens tradeable in small fractions
Small investors can access real estate with minimal capital commitments
Tokenization adds liquidity to traditionally illiquid property investments

faq.question: How does real estate tokenization work in practice?
faq.answer: A property is placed in a legal entity that issues blockchain tokens representing ownership shares. Token holders receive proportional rental income and property value appreciation. Tokens can be traded on secondary markets, providing liquidity. Smart contracts automate income distribution.

faq.question: What barriers prevent widespread adoption of tokenized real estate?
faq.answer: Regulatory frameworks vary by jurisdiction and are still evolving. Secondary markets for tokens lack liquidity in most regions. Legal enforcement of token-based ownership rights is untested. Traditional real estate institutions resist disruption..
